dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4801.text: A fishing net. Formed from 网, with 㓹 indicating the sound; 㓹 is large-seal 銳.

shuowen:4802.text: A fishing net. Formed from 网, with 瓜 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Cast the great net with a splashing sound.”

shuowen:4803.text: A net. Formed from 网, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4804.text: A bent fish-weir and a widow’s fish basket, where fish are detained. Formed from 网 and 畱; 畱 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4805.text: 罜䍡, a fishing net. Formed from 网, with 主 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4806.text: The net 罜䍡. Formed from 网, with 鹿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4807.text: To pile brushwood in water to gather fish. Formed from 网, with 林 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4808.text: To fish with a hook. Formed from 网, with 民 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4809.text: To net birds with silk thread. Formed from 网 and 維. In antiquity the Mang clan first made this net.

shuowen:4810.text: An overturning trap for catching birds. Formed from 网, with 叕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4811.text: An overturning bird trap, 罬. Formed from 网, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4812.text: An overturning trap. Formed from 网, with 包 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The pheasant is caught in the trap.”

shuowen:4813.text: A bird-catching net. Formed from 网, with 𤈫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4814.text: A hare-catching net. Formed from 网, with 否 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4815.text: A net. Formed from 网, with 互 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4816.text: A hare net. Formed from 网, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4817.text: A net within a window. Formed from 网, with 舞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4818.text: To arrange and assign, connecting things as in a net. Formed from 网, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4819.text: To release a guilty person. Formed from 网 and 能: one has worth and ability but falls into the net, then is released. The Rites of Zhou says: “Deliberate on the punishment of the able.”

shuowen:4820.text: To pardon. Formed from 网 and 直.

shuowen:4821.text: To cover. Formed from 网, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4822.text: To curse. Formed from 网 and 言; 网 represents a guilty person.

shuowen:4823.text: To curse. Formed from 网, with 馬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4824.text: A horse’s headstall. Formed from 网 and 𩡧; 𩡧 means horse hobbles.

shuowen:4825.text: A fishing net. Formed from 网, with 或 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4826.text: 罘罳, a screen. Formed from 网, with 思 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4827.text: Sorrow in the heart. Formed from 网; further details are unknown. Ancient writing often also uses 離.

shuowen:4828.text: To cover. Formed from 冂, covered above and below. All characters in this group follow 襾. Read like 𣇩.

shuowen:4829.text: To turn over and over. Formed from 襾, with 乏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4830.text: The truth. In investigating affairs, enclosing, pressing and obstructing a statement until its truth is obtained is 覈. Formed from 襾, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4831.text: To overturn, 覂. Another explanation: to cover. Formed from 襾, with 復 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4832.text: A cloth worn at the belt. Formed from 冂, with 丨 depicting thread. All characters in this group follow 巾.

shuowen:4833.text: Chu calls a large cloth 𢁥. Formed from 巾, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4834.text: A cloth worn at the belt. Formed from 巾 and 𠂤.

shuowen:4835.text: A ceremonial cloth. Formed from 巾 and 執.

shuowen:4836.text: A cloth one width across. Formed from 巾, with 犮 indicating the sound. Read like 撥.

shuowen:4837.text: A pillow cloth. Formed from 巾, with 刃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4838.text: A large cloth covering clothing. Formed from 巾, with 般 indicating the sound. Some take it as a head wrap, 首鞶.

shuowen:4839.text: A lining cloth, 巾帤. Formed from 巾, with 如 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a worn cloth.

shuowen:4840.text: Silk cloth. Formed from 巾, with 敝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4841.text: The width of cloth or silk. Formed from 巾, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4842.text: A coloring craftsman who processes silk and scours it. Formed from 巾, with 𡿬 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 𢂩隔, a covering or partition; the term is uncertain. Read like 荒.

shuowen:4843.text: A sash. Men wear leather belts, women silk ones. Depicts tying on pendants. A pendant must have a cloth, hence 巾.

shuowen:4844.text: Hair covered with a cloth is called 幘. Formed from 巾, with 責 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4845.text: The end of a collar. Formed from 巾, with 旬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4846.text: Hongnong calls a skirt 帔. Formed from 巾, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4847.text: A lower skirt. Formed from 巾, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4848.text: A lower garment. Formed from 巾, with 君 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4849.text: A skirt. Another explanation: a single-width cloth, 帗. Another: a woman’s side garment. Formed from 巾, with 戔 indicating the sound. Read like 殺 in 末殺.

shuowen:4850.text: The garment 𢃭. Formed from 巾, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4851.text: The garment 㡓. Formed from 巾, with 怱 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a book wrapper.

shuowen:4852.text: Chu calls an unhemmed garment 𢅡. Formed from 巾, with 監 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4853.text: A curtain. Formed from 巾, with 冥 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou mentions a “幎 officer.”

shuowen:4854.text: A curtain or canopy. Formed from 巾, with 曼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4855.text: A single-layer curtain. Formed from 巾, with 𠷎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4856.text: A side curtain. Formed from 巾, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4857.text: A curtain at the side is 帷. Formed from 巾, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4858.text: To spread out. Formed from 巾, with 長 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4859.text: A curtain above is 幕; a covering over a food table is also 幕. Formed from 巾, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4860.text: Torn remnants. Formed from 巾, with 匕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4861.text: Remnant silk. Formed from 巾, with 祭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4862.text: To tear neatly across the end. Formed from 巾, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4863.text: A written endorsement on silk. Formed from 巾, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4864.text: A covering for books. Formed from 巾, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4865.text: A banner or standard. Formed from 巾, with 前 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4866.text: A distinguishing mark: red silk attached to the back. Formed from 巾, with abbreviated 微 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Those raising the marks are the duke’s troops.”

shuowen:4867.text: A standard. Formed from 巾, with 𤐫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4868.text: A banner. Formed from 巾, with 夗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4869.text: A cloth used by a writing boy to wipe writing tablets. Formed from 巾, with 番 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4870.text: To brush or sweep off, 刜. Formed from 巾, with 剌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4871.text: To wipe. Formed from 巾, with 韱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4872.text: The worn-out appearance of a cart. Formed from 巾, with 單 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The sandalwood cart is worn out.”

shuowen:4873.text: A covering garment. Formed from 巾, with 冡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4874.text: A canopy covering. Formed from 巾, with 蔑 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a single-layer quilt.

shuowen:4875.text: To cover. Formed from 巾, with 無 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4876.text: To brush. Formed from 巾 and 人, with 食 indicating the sound. Read like 式. Another explanation: adornment.

shuowen:4877.text: A bag. Formed from 巾, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4878.text: A bag; in the present salt administration, three hu make one 帣. Formed from 巾, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4879.text: To sweep away dirt. Formed from 又 holding 巾, sweeping inside 冂. In antiquity Shaokang first made the winnowing basket, broom and millet wine. Shaokang is Dukang, buried at Changyuan.

shuowen:4880.text: A mat. According to the Rites, the Son of Heaven’s and feudal lords’ mats have axe-patterned and embroidered borders. Formed from 巾 and abbreviated 庶.

shuowen:4881.text: A bag. Formed from 巾, with 朕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4882.text: To fill a bag with grain until it is overfull and splits. Formed from 巾, with 奮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4883.text: A container for carrying grain. Formed from 巾, with 盾 indicating the sound. Read like 屯, the Changes hexagram.

shuowen:4884.text: A cattail-mat container. Formed from 巾, with 及 indicating the sound. Read like 蛤.

shuowen:4885.text: Cloth wound around a horse’s bit to fan away sweat. Formed from 巾, with 賁 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The red bit-cloths are splendid.”

shuowen:4886.text: To sweep the ground and wipe it with a cloth. Formed from 巾, with 夒 indicating the sound. Read like 㬮 in 水溫㬮, referring to warm water; the reading phrase is uncertain. Another explanation: to attach.

shuowen:4887.text: Where gold and valuables are stored. Formed from 巾, with 奴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4888.text: Woven hemp. Formed from 巾, with 父 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4889.text: Tribute cloth of the Man and Yi peoples of Nan Commandery. Formed from 巾, with 家 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4890.text: Cloth produced in Donglai. Formed from 巾, with 弦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4891.text: Lacquering cloth. Another explanation: a covering for the crossbar on a cart. Formed from 巾, with 敄 indicating the sound. Read like 頊.

shuowen:4892.text: Lacquering cloth. Formed from 巾, with 辟 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “The mang carriage has a large covering.”

shuowen:4893.text: The end of a collar. Formed from 巾, with 𦔮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4894.text: A kind of banner or standard. Formed from 巾, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4895.text: A kind of banner or standard. Formed from 巾, with 戠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4896.text: A covering above is 帟. Formed from 巾, with 亦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4897.text: A woman’s head ornament. Formed from 巾, with 國 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4898.text: To gather the hair. Formed from 巾, with 喿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4899.text: A bag. Formed from 巾, with 代 indicating the sound. Some forms use 衣.

shuowen:4900.text: Three widths of silk are called 帊. Formed from 巾, with 巴 indicating the sound.
